INDICATION:  ___ year old man with polysubstance abuse admitted w/ multiple rib
fractures subsequently developing hypoxemic resp failure requiring intubation.
Treated briefly for PNA. Also w/ new a-fib w/ RVR and some signs of volume
overload.// Eval for volume or consolidation

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  ___

IMPRESSION: 

Bilateral effusions right greater than left are stable.  Patchy parenchymal
opacities bilaterally right greater than left are also unchanged.  There are
multiple displaced right-sided rib fractures, unchanged.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette is stable.  No pneumothorax is seen.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ETT// eval for interval change      eval for
interval change

IMPRESSION: 

Comparison to ___.  The patient has been extubated.  The lung
volumes have decreased.  Bilateral parenchymal opacities are slightly denser
than on the previous image, the image resembles the 1 taken on ___, at 02:02.  No larger pleural effusions.  Normal size of the heart.

EXAMINATION:  Chest single view

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ETT advanced  2 cm// eval ETT position

TECHNIQUE:  Chest portable AP

COMPARISON:  ___, 10:47, about 45 minutes ago

FINDINGS: 

ET tube has been advanced and now terminates about 2 cm above the bifurcation
of the trachea NG tube is below the diaphragm.  Bilateral lung opacities
unchanged

IMPRESSION: 

Tip of ET tube 2 cm above bifurcation of the trachea

EXAMINATION:  Chest single view

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with et tube// et tube placement

TECHNIQUE:  Chest portable AP

COMPARISON:  ___ 1 hour prior

FINDINGS: 

Tiny right apical pneumothorax persist.  An ET tube has been placed
terminating 4.5 cm above the bifurcation of the trachea.  NG tube is below the
diaphragm.  No change to bilateral opacities.

IMPRESSION: 

Tiny right apical pneumothorax, and bilateral opacities with no interval
change.  Placement of ET tube and NG tube.

EXAMINATION:  Chest single view

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with flail chest// acute resp distress/ SOB

TECHNIQUE:  Chest portable AP

COMPARISON:  ___ 02:02

FINDINGS: 

Right chest tube is out.  There is persistent minute right apical
pneumothorax.  Small right effusion.  Small subcutaneous emphysema on the
right.  Bilateral pulmonary opacities are seen in the more severe on the right
the which is slightly worse than of the previous exam obtained 7 hours
previously.  Also increased is a left lung opacity particularly in the left
midlung field.  There acute changes likely present the pulmonary edema
Bilateral lower lobe atelectasis as previously.

IMPRESSION: 

My new right apical pneumothorax.  Interval increase in bilateral lung
opacities likely due to edema.

EXAMINATION:  Chest single view

INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p blunt chest trauma with R pneumothorax. S/p R
chest tube removal today.// pneumothorax?

TECHNIQUE:  Chest portable AP

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

Right pigtail chest tube has been removed.  There is persistent tiny right
apical pneumothorax.  Pulmonary opacities in the right mid, right lower and
left lower lung fields seen with no significant change compared to the
previous exam.  Subcutaneous emphysema is on the previous study.

IMPRESSION: 

Removal of chest tube with persistent tiny right apical pneumothorax. 
Multifocal lung densities with no interval change.

EXAMINATION:  Chest single view

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with flail chest ___ trauma, chest tube for
hemo/pneumothorax// Assess pleural effusion/pneumothorax/progress with chest
tube drainage

TECHNIQUE:  Chest portable AP

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

There is further decrease to the right apical pneumothorax with only a small
residual present.  Right pigtail catheter in the right hemithorax.  Small
subcutaneous emphysema as previously.  Increased congestion in the right lower
lung field as well as increased opacities in the left base noted as
previously.

IMPRESSION: 

Tiny to small residual right apical pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with R pigtail// eval for interval change

TECHNIQUE:   chest AP

COMPARISON:  ___

IMPRESSION: 

The right-sided pigtail catheter is unchanged.  The right hydropneumothorax is
unchanged.  Subcutaneous emphysema in the right lateral chest wall is also
unchanged.  There is subsegmental atelectasis in the left lung base.  There is
also subsegmental atelectasis in the right lower lobe.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette is stable.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p blunt chest trauma c/b PTX. S/p chest tube
placement on ___. Pneumothorax?// Pneumothorax?     Pneumothorax?

IMPRESSION: 

Compared to chest radiographs since ___ most recently ___ at 20:20.

The volume of the moderate apical component of right pneumothorax unchanged. 
Pigtail pleural drainage catheter unchanged in position projecting over the
lateral right mid chest.  Extensive subcutaneous emphysema has not worsened. 
In the setting of persistent right lower lobe collapse, the volume of right
pleural effusion is difficult to assess, but probably not substantial.  Upper
lungs are clear.  Heterogeneous opacification in the left lower lung could be
atelectasis alone or pneumonia, particularly due to aspiration.

Normal cardiomediastinal and hilar silhouettes.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p R chest tube placement.// Chest tube in good
position? Pneumothorax?

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal chest radiograph

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs, most recently dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Following right chest tube placement, pre-existing moderate right apical
pneumothorax has decreased, now small.  A pre-existing small pleural effusion
has somewhat decreased.  Right basal opacity persists presumably
aspiration/pneumonia.  Retrocardiac opacity is grossly unchanged.  Extensive
subcutaneous emphysema overlying the right chest wall and abdominal wall has
minimally worsened since prior exam obtained 8 hours prior.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette is unchanged.

IMPRESSION:


1. Interval decrease in right apical pneumothorax, now small following chest
tube placement.  Right pleural effusion has minimally decreased, with stable
right basal opacities, likely reflecting aspiration/pneumonia.
2. Unchanged retrocardiac opacity.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with flail chest and ptx// Please eval interval
change      Please eval interval change

IMPRESSION: 

No prior chest radiographs available, despite reference to prior studies in
the request.

Moderate right hydropneumothorax company by substantial lower lobe atelectasis
yields a midline mediastinum.  Heterogeneous opacification left lower lobe
could be either pneumonia or contusion or atelectasis.  Mediastinal contours
are normal, and do not suggest bleeding.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with right-sided pain after a fall in the bathtub, known rib
fractures and pneumothorax on x-ray.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector axial CT images of the chest were obtained without
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were reviewed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 551 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph performed ___ at 10:38

FINDINGS: 

THYROID AND LYMPH NODES: The thyroid is homogeneous in attenuation throughout.
There is no axillary or supraclavicular adenopathy.  Several mediastinal lymph
nodes appear slightly prominent, and are likely reactive.  For instance, there
is a right lower paratracheal node measuring up to 1.1 cm (02:25).  Subcarinal
station node also measures approximately 1 cm (02:29).  Precarinal node
measures 1.1 cm.

HEART AND GREAT VESSELS: Heart is normal in size, without a pericardial
effusion.  Coronary calcifications are noted.  Thoracic aorta is normal in
caliber, with mild atherosclerotic calcifications.

AIRWAYS AND LUNGS: There are dependent secretions in the proximal thoracic
trachea (03:32) and proximal right mainstem bronchus (03:45).  Diffuse
bronchial wall thickening with scattered areas of mucous plugging are most
notable at the lung bases.  There is biapical pleuroparenchymal scarring. 
Multifocal scattered areas of ___ and nodular opacities are noted,
suggestive of an inflammatory process such as from aspiration or potentially
superimposed infection. Notable representative examples are as follows: right
upper lobe (3:79), right lower lobe (3:82), left upper lobe (03:58) and left
lower lobe (3:84).  Dense consolidation right lung base consolidation is
likely part of the same process (3:95).

PLEURA: There is a small right pneumothorax, and small effusion on the right. 
No pneumothorax or pleural effusion on the left.

BONES: Multiple right-sided rib fractures are noted.  There is slight
angulation of the right anterolateral fourth rib, although no discrete
fracture line is identified (3:67).  Mildly displaced fracture of the
anterolateral fifth rib.  Acute fractures of the right sixth, seventh, eighth,
ninth and tenth ribs are completely displaced by a cortex width.  Acute
fracture of the right posterior eleventh rib is nondisplaced (3:100).  There
is adjacent soft tissue edema and likely pleural-based hematoma, most notable
adjacent to the posterior tenth rib (4:181).  No acute thoracic spine fracture
is identified.

SOFT TISSUES: Evaluation of the soft tissues is notable for extensive
subcutaneous emphysema along the right lateral chest wall, extending
inferiorly towards the upper lateral abdominal wall.

UPPER ABDOMEN: There is a 3 mm nonobstructing stone in the upper pole of the
left kidney (605:61).

IMPRESSION:


1. Multiple consecutive acute fractures involving the ___ through 11th ribs,
all of which are displaced except for the eleventh rib.
2. Small right pneumothorax.  Small nonhemorrhagic right pleural effusion.
3. Areas of airway mucous plugging with multifocal ___ and nodular
parenchymal opacities as described above, suspicious for aspiration or
pneumonia.
4. Prominent mediastinal lymph nodes are likely reactive.
5. 3mm non-obstruction left renal stone.

NOTIFICATION:  The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by ___
___, M.D. in person on ___ at 1:40 pm, 2 minutes after discovery of the
findings.

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with rib fx, subq air// ? Rib fx ? Pneumothorax

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images obtained through the cervical spine
without intravenous contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformats were reviewed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 5.8 s, 22.8 cm; CTDIvol = 22.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 517.2
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 517 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Alignment is normal.  No fractures are identified.Degenerative changes include
intervertebral disc height loss, posterior osteophytes and uncovertebral joint
hypertrophy most notably at C5-C6 resulting in moderate bilateral foraminal
narrowing.  Disc bulges at C3-4 and C4-5 efface the ventral CSF.There is no
prevertebral edema.

The thyroid is unremarkable.  Mucosal thickening noted in the partially
visualized maxillary sinuses.  Left mastoid tip is partially opacified with
adjacent sclerosis suggesting chronic inflammation.

Right apical pneumothorax and subcutaneous gas, better assessed on concurrent
chest CT.

IMPRESSION: 

Degenerative changes without fracture or malalignment.

EXAMINATION:  CT L-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ s/p fall now w tenderness at T-spine   scoliosis// ?trauma   
?trauma

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast helical multidetector CT was performed through the
lumbar spine.  Soft tissue and bone algorithm images were generated.  Coronal
and sagittal reformations were then constructed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 7.3 s, 28.8 cm; CTDIvol = 31.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 891.8
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 892 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is bilateral L5 spondylolysis with grade 2 anterolisthesis of L5 on S1. 
Vertebral bodies are preserved in height and they are otherwise preserved in
alignment.  There is no fracture.

Anterolisthesis results in severe bilateral L5-S1 neuroforaminal narrowing. 
Otherwise, no significant canal or foraminal narrowing.

Mild atherosclerotic calcifications noted in the abdominal aorta which is
otherwise unremarkable.  There is a nonobstructing 4 mm calculus within the
left kidney.  Other included paraspinal and retroperitoneal soft tissues are
unremarkable.  There is no significant canal or foraminal narrowing.

IMPRESSION:


1. No fracture or traumatic malalignment.
2. Bilateral L5 spondylolysis with grade 2 anterolisthesis of L5 on S1.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ with hypoxia after a fall with chest wall injury.  Evaluate
for fracture or pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable chest radiograph

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Opacification of the right lung base may represent atelectasis or contusion in
the setting of trauma.  There is suggestion of the small right apical
pneumothorax given lack of parenchymal markings at the apex and possible
pleural reflection.  Left lung is essentially clear.  No sizable pleural
effusion.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits.  There are
displaced rib fractures on the right, likely involving the lateral ___,
___ and likely ninth ribs.  Evaluation of the soft tissues is notable for
associated subcutaneous emphysema.

IMPRESSION:


1. Acute displaced fractures likely involving at least the right lateral ___,
___ and likely 9th ribs, with associated subcutaneous emphysema.
2. Probable small right apical pneumothorax.
3. Right lung base atelectasis versus contusion.

NOTIFICATION:  The findings were discussed with Dr.  ___. by ___
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 12:05 pm, 2 minutes after
discovery of the findings.
